B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The reviewed sources did not establish a price, usage quota, or per-call fee for MCP. The Admin MCP documentation describes project access and permission prerequisites.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An interactive OAuth session is required for write operations. Project-scoped connections are limited to granted projects; organization-wide connections can access projects in that organization. Dashboard permissions govern actions. Credentials can read but cannot change content. Redirect domains can be configured in MCP settings.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs describe read and write operations, including destructive delete/discard operations. Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published in the reviewed docs. 2. Server-enforced checks include OAuth, scopes, project roles, branch requirements, and a required OAuth principal for write/comment/branch/publish/discard operations; human approval is required to accept/reject tracked suggestions in the editor. The docs also recommend reviewing large diffs. 3. OAuth scopes are listed in C. Permissions inherit Mintlify dashboard roles and granted project scope; credentials are read-only. Organization admins configure redirect domains and credentials. Token expiry/revocation details were not found. 4. Admin MCP is distinct from the read/search-only site Search MCP endpoint at /mcp. Branch argument determines target branch; project management changes apply immediately to the live project. No request-level read-only filter was documented. 5. Private pages have visibility and role checks; private-page access rejects client and machine-to-machine tokens. No field-level masking or PII exclusion documented. 6. list_nodes pagination uses opaque cursors; edits can accept up to 100 replacements per call; multi-project reads accept up to 25 projects; analytics results paginate. No general rate or cost limit found. 7. Docs describe validation errors and failures, including navigationErrors, notRendered and no_match/not_unique; no parameter auto-correction documented. 8. General privacy/terms describe processing and security, but MCP-specific audit logging and telemetry details were not found. 9. get_analytics_report includes feedback reports, but no agent-facing feedback/rating tool or upsell behavior was found in the official tool list. 10. Separate Codex plugin distributes an external skill; no server-delivered skill tool documented. The guidance to review diffs is advisory. 11. Server does not remember a branch between calls; the client passes branch each time. Other behavior memory not documented. 12. Two distinct official surfaces exist: Admin MCP and site Search MCP; the input endpoint is the Admin MCP. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool appears in the official tool list. query_analytics is documented as read-only SELECT.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Before merging, read the PR diff and skim the rendered preview. Don’t rubber-stamp large changes.
If your project requires a pull request, Mintlify refuses the edit with a message that explains why and changes nothing. Call create_branch and pass the returned branchName as branch instead.
You can reply to suggestion threads, but you must accept or reject suggestions in the editor.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Mintlify documents separate Admin MCP and Search MCP endpoints with different audiences, permissions, and tool sets. The input endpoint is the hosted Admin MCP.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official Admin MCP tool reference exists at https://www.mintlify.com/docs/ai/mintlify-mcp. Extracted 38 distinct names from its documented tool descriptions; no official total was stated. actions.json contains these names. The Claude connector directory lists a 15-tool subset (checkout, save, discard_session, read, search, list_nodes, get_session_state, diff, edit_page, write_page, create_node, update_node, move_node, delete_node, update_config) and describes the connector as partner-listed; those names differ from or are absent in the current official reference and were not added. Runlayer reports 35 captured tools, including proxy/catalogue-only entries such as execute_code and agent_review_settings; its list conflicts with current official documentation and was not treated as the authoritative list. Other catalogues provide varying or incomplete summaries.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Humans can accept or reject tracked suggestions in the dashboard editor; the docs say the agent can propose suggestions but acceptance or rejection occurs in the editor. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs advise: “Before merging, read the PR diff and skim the rendered preview. Don’t rubber-stamp large changes.” This is client/user guidance; no server enforcement is described.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The docs state credentials can read content but cannot change it, and edits to tracked suggestions do not change the page until accepted or rejected in the dashboard editor. The terms say Mintlify uses commercially reasonable efforts to maintain security and integrity of the service and customer data.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Mintlify describes project-scoped access, permission checks, branch-aware editing, and updated state returned by project-management write tools.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth, project scopes, roles, branch requirements, and credential write restrictions are documented as server-enforced. The large-diff review recommendation is advisory. Suggestion acceptance/rejection is a product workflow performed in the dashboard. General security language is contractual and does not specify MCP-specific logging or telemetry.

contradictions: The Claude connector directory lists 15 tools, including checkout, save, and discard_session, while the current official tool reference documents a different, broader list and names discard rather than discard_session. The catalogue subset is not a complete match for the official reference.
Runlayer reports 35 captured tools and includes execute_code and agent_review_settings, which were not found in the official reference. These catalogue-only names were not included in actions.json.

OAuth metadata advertises write scopes for billing, integrations, and sessions, but the reviewed official Admin MCP tool reference did not document corresponding billing-write or integration-write tools.
observations_for_research: The Admin MCP combines project-scoped OAuth with dashboard-role checks and a separate read-only credential mode.
Content edits are branch-aware, while project-management writes apply directly to the live project.
Tracked suggestions preserve a human acceptance step, while other documented write tools can alter project content or settings.
notes: Reviewed the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ index and collected official docs, blog, legal pages, catalogues and the local codex-plugin repository. The public repository is not server implementation code. The 38 extracted names come from official tool-description text; schemas and complete parameter definitions were not published in the extracted reference, so actions.json marks parameters NOT PUBLISHED. No token estimate could be computed without tools/list or server code. The official pricing page and legal pages were checked; no MCP-specific price was established. Unofficial/community server evidence was not used.
